claim: Eteplirsen improves clinical outcomes in Duchenne muscular dystrophy
gold_rationale: Clinical/regulatory consensus is that a clinical-outcome benefit of eteplirsen in DMD is UNPROVEN. FDA granted accelerated approval in Sept 2016 (EXONDYS 51) solely on a DYSTROPHIN SURROGATE endpoint that CDER Director Woodcock judged 'reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit' — over the formal dissent of the review team (Unger at Office level, Bastings at Division level, DNP), a scientific-dispute appeal (Unger->Borio->Califf), and a split/negative advisory committee (7-6 against accelerated approval on the surrogate question; 7-3 with 3 abstentions that the Study 201/202 clinical data did NOT provide substantial evidence of effectiveness), with an explicit confirmatory-clinical-outcome-trial requirement. The pivotal randomized double-blind trial (Study 201, PMID 23907995) enrolled only n=12 (4/group) and did NOT meet its primary clinical endpoint (change in 6MWT at week 24); the cited 67.3 m 'benefit' is a post-hoc ambulation-evaluable comparison vs delayed/placebo patients. Longer-term 6MWT/ambulation advantages (PMID 26573217: 151 m at 36 mo; PMID 33523015: 159 m at year 4) derive from non-randomized matched historical/external controls the FDA review team judged unreliable (no patient clearly deviated from natural history). PROMOVI (NCT02255552 / PMID 34120909) was open-label and its concurrent untreated control was deemed inappropriate, so it too rests on post-hoc external-control comparisons. The measured dystrophin increase was tiny (mean ~0.3% of normal, from ~0.22% to ~0.32%; range 0-1.3%), an order of magnitude below the ~10% level thought clinically relevant. An adequately powered randomized dose-comparison confirmatory trial (NCT03992430, NSAA primary, primary completion ~2026) remained ongoing/unread-out as of cutoff. Therefore evidence for CLINICAL benefit is Insufficient — approval turns on a surrogate, not demonstrated clinical efficacy. Note: the FDA (Califf/Unger) formally urged retraction of the Study 201 paper as 'misleading'; Annals of Neurology declined and the paper carries no retraction/erratum mark.
outcome: clinical/functional outcome (6-minute walk distance, ambulation/loss of ambulation, forced vital capacity, North Star Ambulatory Assessment)
population: Ambulatory (and some non-ambulatory) boys with genetically confirmed DMD carrying deletion mutations amenable to exon-51 skipping (~13% of the DMD population)
provenance: PubMed (Ann Neurol, Neurology, J Neuromuscul Dis) + ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT02255552, NCT03992430) + FDA CDER NDA 206488 decisional/appeal memoranda (Woodcock 2016-07-14, Unger Office+appeal, Borio 2016-08-08, Califf 2016-09-16) and Advisory Committee record; Retraction Watch documentation of the failed retraction request.
notes: Surrogate detection is decisive: FDA approval is explicitly surrogate-based (dystrophin protein), and every functional-outcome signal comes from either a primary-endpoint FAILURE (Study 201 6MWT) or from non-randomized historical/external-control comparisons. No adequately powered RCT has demonstrated a clinical-outcome benefit as of cutoff. dramatic_effect is FALSE for all rows: the effect is small, the primary clinical endpoint failed, and controlled data do not show an all-or-none benefit. Verifier corrections applied: PROMOVI design rct->prospective cohort (open-label, control rejected); FDA row source_id corrected from the paper DOI to the FDA NDA 206488 docket; PMID 23907995 integrity_note augmented to disclose the FDA-led (unsuccessful) retraction request while keeping integrity_ok=true since the paper is not actually retracted.

baseline.text: Eteplirsen (EXONDYS 51) has NOT been shown to improve clinical outcomes in Duchenne muscular dystrophy in an adequately powered controlled trial. FDA granted it accelerated approval in 2016 based only on a surrogate endpoint — a small increase in dystrophin protein — which the agency judged reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit, over the objection of its own review team and a divided advisory committee. The pivotal randomized trial had just 12 patients and did not meet its primary 6-minute-walk endpoint; claimed functional benefits rest largely on comparisons to historical controls rather than randomized data. Clinical benefit remains unproven and controversial pending a confirmatory trial.

rows.citation: Mendell JR, et al. Eteplirsen for the treatment of Duchenne muscular dystrophy. Ann Neurol. 2013;74(5):637-47. DOI:10.1002/ana.23982
rows.integrity_note: Pivotal double-blind placebo-controlled trial (Study 201), n=12 (4/group) — severely underpowered. Primary clinical endpoint (change in 6MWT at week 24) was NOT met per FDA review; the reported 67.3 m advantage is a post-hoc ambulation-evaluable comparison vs placebo/delayed patients after unblinding. Headline result is the DYSTROPHIN SURROGATE (23%/52% dystrophin-positive fibers), not a clinical outcome. Integrity caveat: FDA Commissioner Califf and Dr. Unger formally urged Annals of Neurology to correct/retract this paper as 'misleading' (unreliable dystrophin assay); per Retraction Watch the journal declined — no retraction and no formal erratum was issued, so the paper carries no PubMed mark and remains citable (integrity_ok=true), but the FDA-disputed status is noted.
rows.finding: Randomized n=12 trial: eteplirsen raised dystrophin-positive fibers (surrogate) but did NOT meet its primary clinical 6MWT endpoint at 24 weeks; functional signal is post-hoc/underpowered — direction on the CLAIMED clinical outcome is null. FDA later contested the paper's reliability (retraction requested, not granted).

rows.citation: Charleston JS, et al. Eteplirsen treatment for Duchenne muscular dystrophy: Exon skipping and dystrophin production. Neurology. 2018;90(24):e2146-e2154. DOI:10.1212/WNL.0000000000005680
rows.integrity_note: Open-label observational extension (Study 202); endpoint is the dystrophin SURROGATE only (Western blot, immunofluorescence, PDPF), not a clinical/functional outcome. Confirms exon skipping and dystrophin increase vs untreated controls; says nothing about clinical benefit. Sarepta-affiliated authorship.
rows.finding: Confirms mechanism — exon-51 skipping and a small dystrophin protein increase vs untreated controls — but measures only the SURROGATE, providing no evidence on the claimed clinical outcome.

rows.citation: Mendell JR, et al. Longitudinal effect of eteplirsen versus historical control on ambulation in Duchenne muscular dystrophy. Ann Neurol. 2016;79(2):257-71. DOI:10.1002/ana.24555
rows.integrity_note: Reports a 151 m 6MWT advantage at 36 months (n=12 eteplirsen vs n=13 matched historical controls), but the comparator is MATCHED HISTORICAL CONTROLS, not randomized. FDA review team judged such non-randomized comparisons unreliable and concluded no patient clearly deviated from natural history. Sarepta-affiliated authors; small n.
rows.finding: Non-randomized historical-control comparison suggesting slower 6MWT decline with eteplirsen (151 m advantage at 36 mo) — a real functional-outcome signal, but confounded by external-control design that regulators deemed unreliable.

rows.citation: Mendell JR, et al. Comparison of Long-term Ambulatory Function in Patients with DMD Treated with Eteplirsen and Matched Natural History Controls. J Neuromuscul Dis. 2021;8(4):469-479. DOI:10.3233/JND-200548
rows.integrity_note: Retrospective matched external-control study (Study 201/202 n=12 vs Italian Telethon/Leuven registries). Reports 159 m 6MWT advantage at Year 4 and higher proportion ambulant (10/12 vs 3/11), but is non-randomized, retrospective, and Sarepta-funded — same external-control confound flagged by FDA.
rows.finding: Retrospective matched-control analysis again favoring eteplirsen on 6MWT and ambulation at 4 years, but the non-randomized external-control design cannot establish clinical benefit.

rows.citation: PROMOVI (Study 301). Open-Label Study With a Concurrent Untreated Control Arm to Evaluate Efficacy and Safety of Eteplirsen in DMD. Sarepta Therapeutics. ClinicalTrials.gov NCT02255552 (published: McDonald CM, et al. J Neuromuscul Dis. 2021;8(6):989-1001, PMID:34120909, DOI:10.3233/JND-210643)
rows.integrity_note: Phase 3 but OPEN-LABEL, effectively single-arm for efficacy: the pre-specified concurrent untreated cohort (not amenable to exon 51 skipping) was deemed an 'inappropriate control group' due to genotype-driven trajectory differences, so efficacy claims fall back to POST-HOC external natural-history comparisons. 78/79 eteplirsen patients completed 96 weeks; total enrollment 109 (79 treated + 30 untreated). Not a valid controlled test of clinical benefit; Sarepta-sponsored. Corrected from 'rct' to 'prospective cohort' by verifier.
rows.finding: Largest eteplirsen study (n=79 treated): its own concurrent control was rejected as inappropriate, leaving only post-hoc external-control 6MWT/FVC comparisons — no valid controlled demonstration of clinical outcome.

rows.citation: MIS51ON. Randomized, Double-Blind, Dose-Finding and Comparison Study of High-Dose Eteplirsen in DMD Amenable to Exon 51 Skipping (confirmatory trial). Sarepta Therapeutics. ClinicalTrials.gov NCT03992430
rows.integrity_note: The adequately powered randomized double-blind confirmatory/dose-comparison trial (n~160; NSAA total-score primary endpoint at Week 144, interim at Week 72/96). Status ACTIVE_NOT_RECRUITING with primary completion ~2026-10-31 as of retrieval — no read-out clinical-outcome result available at knowledge cutoff. Sarepta-sponsored.
rows.finding: The adequately powered randomized confirmatory clinical-outcome trial required for approval verification remained ongoing/unread-out — the key evidence that would resolve clinical benefit does not yet exist.

rows.citation: FDA CDER, NDA 206488 (EXONDYS 51 / eteplirsen) — Center Director Decisional Memorandum (Woodcock, 2016-07-14), Office of Drug Evaluation-I Decisional Memo + SDR Appeal (Unger), Chief Scientist SDR summary (Borio, 2016-08-08), Commissioner decision (Califf, 2016-09-16); accelerated approval granted 2016-09-19. accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2016/206488Orig1s000.
rows.integrity_note: Authoritative regulatory record. Approval was ACCELERATED, based ONLY on the dystrophin SURROGATE (statistically significant Study 301 increase ~0.22%->0.32% of normal; mean ~0.3%, range 0-1.3%), an order of magnitude below the ~10% level Unger/Borio judged needed for clinical relevance. Review team (Unger/Bastings/DNP/Biometrics/Clin-Pharm) recommended Complete Response; Advisory Committee voted 7-6 against accelerated approval on the surrogate question and 7-3 (3 abstentions) that Study 201/202 clinical data did not provide substantial evidence of effectiveness. Clinical benefit was explicitly NOT established; confirmatory clinical-outcome trial required. All figures independently verified verbatim against the FDA memoranda. (Verifier corrected source_id from the reused paper DOI to the FDA NDA 206488 docket.)
rows.finding: FDA regulatory consensus: eteplirsen approved on a dystrophin surrogate only (~0.3% of normal), with clinical benefit explicitly UNPROVEN and a confirmatory outcome trial required — contradicts the claim that clinical outcomes are established (direction -1).
